items.text: Our latest performance update is now available to all players on Steam, following testing on the public beta branch.

Independent hardware testing recorded an average frame-rate improvement of around 34%, with improvements seen on 21 of the 22 systems tested. Results will vary depending on your hardware, graphics settings and what’s happening in-game.
We know performance has been a frustration for many of you. If it’s kept you from enjoying Mechanicus II, we hope this update gives you a reason to return.

Thank you to everyone who tried the beta and shared feedback. Please let us know how the update runs for you, and report any issues through the bug report form, including your system specifications and graphics settings.
Hi everyone.
While we continue work on the next update, we’ve made a new build available on the optional public_beta branch on Steam.

This build includes further work aimed at improving game performance. Our internal testing across a range of hardware has been very encouraging, but PC performance can vary considerably between different systems, so we’d like to test the update more widely before considering a full public release.

If you’ve previously experienced poor performance in Mechanicus II, we’d particularly appreciate you trying the beta and letting us know whether you see an improvement, no meaningful change, or any new issues.
For feedback and bug reports, please use our bug report form. Where relevant, please include your CPU, GPU, resolution, graphics settings and whether you’re using DirectX 11 or DirectX 12.
Right-click Warhammer 40,000: Mechanicus II in your Steam Library.
Select Properties.
Open the Betas tab.
Enter mechanicus2beta into the private beta access code field and select Check Code.
Select public_beta under Beta Participation.
Steam should then automatically download the build.
To return to the current public version, select None from the same menu.

This new bug fix update focuses on confirmed gameplay, progression, stability, visual, and localisation issues reported since release. This includes fixes for several mission blockers, crashes and combat or skill-related problems, alongside a new setting intended to reduce CPU load on some systems.

We know some players are still waiting for further improvements to performance and other technical issues, this update is not intended to address that. The broader optimisation work continues separately and we'll share updates on that as soon as we can.
You can find the full list of changes below. The changelog is available in English only.
Fixed missions becoming impossible to start after investing in Scaevola’s Eradication Ray upgrades while she had numerous active perks.
Fixed the Forge City Assault mission failing to trigger after awakening all three tombs surrounding Zeocene.
Fixed the Mission Failure screen not appearing when Faustinius was defeated during the final skirmish of Jaws of Defeat.
Fixed Command Protocols disappearing after loading an autosave during the final skirmish of Regicide.
Fixed a brief freeze when the Lokhust Heavy Destroyer used the Enmitic Exterminator.
Fixed a crash that could occur when a Tesla Carbine attack struck destructible scenery.
Fixed Killcycle Canticle granting Multiple Uses on the first use of Invocation of Machine Vengeance and not stacking correctly after repeated uses.
Updated Videx’s Ritual description to clarify that allied units cannot activate Canticles while the Ritual is being performed.
Updated Machine Spirit Resurgent to clarify that Accelerated is only applied to units within 5 tiles when its Data-choir condition is met.
Updated the description of Accelerated to remove an incorrect numerical value.
Updated Videx’s upgrade text to clarify that only Videx’s Rituals cost 1 fewer CP to conduct.
Fixed the Battleware Override trait tooltip not appearing when highlighting Scaevola’s Battleware Override upgrade.
Fixed the first passive trait appearing twice in the recruitment details of multiple Tech-Priests.
Fixed Fulgurite Electro-Priests being unable to attack Canoptek Spyders from diagonally adjacent positions.
Fixed Hexmark Destroyer attacks failing to generate Dominion from damage dealt.
Fixed corrupted characters appearing in the Simplified Chinese localisation.
Implemented missing French translations in the Lord’s Chamber interface.
Fixed unit names being incorrectly aligned when characters appeared on the right side of dialogue conversations.
Fixed bright visual artefacts appearing in certain skirmish maps and cutscenes.
Added a new Cloth Quality setting designed to reduce CPU load on some systems.

releases.displayName: Performance Update – Unity Upgrade, New Graphics Settings and Bug Fixes

items.text: Hi everyone.
Today, we’re releasing a major technical update for Warhammer 40,000: Mechanicus II, built around an upgrade to a newer version of Unity.

Internal testing and feedback from the public beta of this build indicate that the upgrade improves baseline performance and optimisation across a wide range of hardware configurations. However, performance gains will vary depending on your system and settings, and we want to be clear that some players may see limited or no noticeable improvement from the engine upgrade alone.
To provide greater control over performance, the update also introduces two new graphics settings:
Mesh LOD Quality: Controls the level of detail used for 3D models at a distance. Reducing this setting may improve performance, particularly during larger or more visually demanding skirmishes.
Background Effects: Controls the visual effects displayed in the backgrounds of environments. Reducing or disabling these effects may improve performance in affected areas.
We recommend experimenting with these settings to find the best balance between visual quality and performance for your system.

We have also added a much-requested option to restart a mission from the War Map before it is launched. This allows you to reconsider your deployment and select a different leader or force without needing to reload an earlier save.
Our support for the game is continuing, and we will keep reviewing player feedback and investigating reported issues following this release. Please look forward to future news and updates.

Thank you to everyone who has submitted bug reports, tested the public beta or shared detailed feedback with us. Your reports have been extremely valuable in helping us identify issues, verify fixes and prioritise our ongoing work. We also greatly appreciate your continued patience and support.
Alongside the Unity upgrade, new graphics options and mission restart feature, this update contains a large number of bug fixes. You can find the full changelog (English only) below.
Fixed an issue that could cause campaign saves to become stuck on an infinite loading screen after completing a mission.
Fixed an issue during Vindication where the Deceiver seemingly failed to return after using Grand Illusion, preventing the final skirmish from progressing.
Fixed an issue where manual saves could disappear after relaunching the game, and loading an older save could remove newer autosave checkpoints.
Fixed a softlock that could occur when multiple Matrix Explosion effects resolved simultaneously and killed the currently active unit.
Fixed a softlock that could occur when a Corpuscarii Electro-Priest’s attacks were blocked.
Fixed an issue where Hyperspace Hunter could teleport a Deathmark into an inaccessible area, preventing the skirmish from being completed.
Fixed a freeze that could occur when moving a Kataphron Destroyer immediately after deployment during the final skirmish of The Jaws of Defeat.
Fixed an issue where a unit could become unselectable after ending its movement on a corpse.
Fixed an issue that could result in an infinite loading screen around Territory Expansion missions.
Fixed a freeze that could occur when retrying a mission with a different leader after abandoning it following Scaevola’s death.
Fixed a Necron campaign progression block after Oszereon where no activities remained available to advance time.
Fixed a potential softlock that could occur in the final skirmish of Pontifex Maximus.
Destroyed Forge Cities will no longer reappear as available Forge City Assault targets.
Fixed an issue where successfully defending a Forge-Temple could still result in its destruction and prevent queued construction or upgrades from completing.
The Necron Lord’s upgraded Resurrection Orb can now correctly target eligible units undergoing Reanimation Protocol after reaching Dominion level 8.
Triarch Praetorians can no longer use Judgement From On High while Immobilised.
Treasure of the Technomandrites now correctly buffs the Warscythe and Voidscythe.
Grav-wave Shock Mines now reliably stop affected enemy units when triggered.
The Arc Pistol can now correctly damage environmental objects.
Khepra’s Cantic Thrallnet now causes affected enemy units to activate according to the updated turn order.
Videx’s movement now correctly ignores damaging ground effects, including burning ground.
Videx’s Optimised Benediction upgrade now correctly reduces the cost of Benediction of Omniscience for Fulgurite Electro-Priests.
Khepra’s Servo-skull now correctly grants Cognition when its effect is applied to an enemy unit.
The Sicarian Infiltrator Princeps’ Servo-skull and Kill Analysis effects now correctly grant Cognition when the marked target is killed.
The Sicarian Infiltrator’s Arc Grenade now correctly damages Canoptek Scarab Swarms and Wraiths.
Faustinus can no longer repeatedly refresh his weapon uses by using Dominus Spatial Alternator.
Captrix’s movement Canticle will no longer become permanently unavailable following attacks of opportunity.
Fixed the interaction between Scaevola’s Master of Xenarite Technology and the self-damage caused by Dirge of the Steel.
The Kastelan Robot’s Phosphor Blaster now correctly benefits from Energised.
The Technomancer skill now correctly reduces the remaining Reanimation Protocol cooldown.
Enemy Skitarii and Necron units encountered during Starvation will now engage each other as intended.
Fixed an issue where purchasing Refined Bionics II did not increase the ranks of available units.
The Wraith Form tooltip now correctly describes the skill’s Dominion scaling, including its Dominion level 10 range and damage increases.
Skorpekh units affected by Eternal Revenant now immediately revive when killed by Burning or Irradiated effects.
Captrix’s Omniscrambler now correctly applies Final Data-whisper to allied units rather than enemy units.
Scaevola’s Contamination upgrade no longer allows Devoured From Within to transfer to Scaevola.
Videx’s Electro Incantation now correctly reduces the Cognition cost of Incantation of the Iron Soul for both Corpuscarii and Fulgurite Electro-Priests.
Captrix’s Dodge and Improved Dodge effects now apply correctly.
Hehki can no longer generate Dominion during deployment by repeatedly applying statuses through Quantum Reanimytes.
The Lokhust Heavy Destroyer’s final Gauss Destructor pierce upgrade now works correctly when beginning a mission with 3 locked Dominion.
Videx’s locked Motive Force Ritual skills can no longer be used during skirmishes before being unlocked from the Reliquary.
Radial Suffusion Field now correctly transfers Irradiated when a unit dies from the status.
Rho’s Machine Harmony upgrade now correctly applies the bonus Data-Choir stack.
Videx’s Remote Prognostication upgrade now correctly allows Auto-Divinatory Parchments to target eligible allied units.
Fixed several mission descriptions and dialogue lines that were not displayed in Korean during the Necron campaign.
Fixed untranslated English text appearing in the Lord’s Chamber interface.
Fixed inconsistent turn durations displayed for Construct a Forgeworks between the action description and character portrait.
Fixed an issue where destroying a Forge City during the Necron campaign could trigger incorrect Adeptus Mechanicus post-mission dialogue.
Adjusted certain battlefield ambient tracks that could drown out gameplay sound effects.
Fixed an issue where Deathmark’s legs could flip backwards during certain animations.
Fixed an issue where Epilogue Unlocked! could fail to unlock after completing both campaigns.

releases.displayName: Performance Update Available on Beta Branch

items.text: Hello everyone.

As previously mentioned, the team is currently working on a performance-focused update for Warhammer 40,000: Mechanicus II. This build includes a major engine update, with the aim of delivering meaningful performance and optimisation improvements.

The build is still undergoing testing on our side. However, because PC performance can vary significantly depending on hardware, drivers, settings, Steam cache state and other system-specific factors, we also want to gather feedback from a wider range of real player setups before moving the update to the main live branch.
For that reason, we’re making the upcoming performance update available through an optional public Steam beta branch.
This will allow players who are currently experiencing performance issues, or who simply want to help test the build, to try it ahead of the full release and share feedback with us.
Beta Branch Details
Branch name: public_beta
Branch password: mechanicus2beta

notes.title: Instructions on how to access the branch

items.text: Right-click Warhammer 40,000: Mechanicus II in your Steam Library.
Select Properties.
Go to Betas.
Enter the beta access code above.
Select the beta branch from the dropdown once it appears.
Allow Steam to update the game.
To return to the current live version, go back to the Betas menu and select None.
This is an optional beta branch, not the default live version of the game.
The build is still in testing and may contain issues or regressions.
We’re not asking all players to switch over – only those who are comfortable testing a work-in-progress build.
The current live branch will remain available as normal.
Feedback from the beta will help us better understand performance across a wider range of hardware before the update is released fully.
Reporting Performance Issues
If on the beta branch you continue to experience severe optimisation or performance issues, please report them through our existing bug report form (https://forms.gle/L6JrusUkoSzaZU5PA).
When reporting performance issues, please include as much detail as possible, especially:
your hardware specifications
a DxDiag file, where possible
your in-game graphics settings
the mission/skirmish where the issue occurred
whether performance changed compared to the current live build
whether you had previously cleared your Steam shader/cache files on your local machine

Thank you again for your patience and for continuing to share detailed reports with us. We know the current performance issues have been frustrating, and we want to make sure this update is tested as thoroughly as possible before it becomes the main live build.

releases.displayName: We Hear You – Bug Fix Update and Ongoing Optimisation Work

items.text: First, thank you to everyone who has reported issues and shared feedback since the launch of Warhammer 40,000: Mechanicus II.

We know we’ve been quiet since launch. That hasn’t been because we’re ignoring the issues being raised – it’s because the team has been focused on investigating, fixing and preparing updates as quickly as possible.

We’re painfully aware that many players are experiencing performance issues, including lower than expected frame rates and unusually high GPU utilisation. Improving performance is a critical priority for us, and work is continuing on a more substantial optimisation update.

Today’s update addresses a number of commonly reported bugs and includes a small FPS improvement for many players. However, we want to be clear that this update is not intended to resolve the main performance concerns raised by players. That work is ongoing and will require a further update.
We understand how frustrating these issues are, and we appreciate your patience while we work to address them. We’ll share more details on the optimisation update as soon as we’re able.
Update 1.0.0.25 Patch Notes
General
Implemented a change that results in a slight FPS improvement for many players.
Fixed an issue where the Shadow Quality setting could reset to High after relaunching the game.
Fixed a missing placeholder icon for some skills.
Fixed an issue preventing certain territory expansion missions in the Adeptus Mechanicus campaign from loading.
Audio
Fixed a number of SFX being incorrectly tied to VO volume.
Fixed some missing VO dialogue.
Fixed some instances of dialogue being wrongly assigned to different characters..
Gameplay
Fixed an issue where Videx’s Motive Force skill could grant an incorrect number of Energized stacks.
Fixed an issue in the Vindication skirmish where reaching the extraction area before killing all enemies could incorrectly result in a defeat.
Fixed an issue where triggering a Kastelan Robot’s Deadly Demise trait could skip allied unit turns and disrupt turn order.
Fixed an issue where recruiting a high number of units for a mission (19+) could prevent units from being deployed into a skirmish.
Fixed an issue where the Necron Deathmark Skill Improvement upgrade increased the cooldown of Hyper-dimensional Jump instead of reducing it.
Fixed an issue where the Expanded Sicarian Armour tooltip could obscure the upgrade button and prevent the upgrade from being selected.
Fixed an issue where Nanoscarab Cloud did not gain an additional use at Dominion 8.
Fixed an issue where The Hungry Void command protocol did not apply to the Voidblade.
Fixed an issue where multiple units could be deployed onto the same cell during the deployment phase.
Fixed an issue where Pteraxii Sterylizors had access to Purgation Protocol before unlocking it.
Fixed an issue where A Call for Flesh could sometimes fail to spawn a Flayed One.
Fixed an issue where Khepra’s Emergency Protocol skill could not be activated after being unlocked.
Achievements
Fixed an issue where the Tech-Acquisitor achievement could fail to unlock after reaching 10 Cognition Points with Scaevola.
Fixed an issue on Xbox where the achievement notification pop-up did not display correctly.
